servers.name: Blender MCP
servers.summary: Drive Blender from an LLM: inspect the scene and objects, capture a viewport screenshot, run arbitrary Python inside Blender, and pull assets from PolyHaven, Sketchfab, Hyper3D Rodin and Hunyuan3D. The server talks over a local socket (localhost:9876) to a companion addon that must be installed and started inside a running Blender.
servers.title: Blender
servers.tagline: Build and change 3D scenes in Blender by asking.

servers.name: Brave Search MCP
servers.summary: Brave Search API integration: web, local, images, videos, news, and summarization
servers.title: Brave Search
servers.tagline: Search the web, news, images and videos with Brave Search.

servers.name: CalDAV Calendar
servers.summary: Calendar access over CalDAV: list, create, update and delete events and reminders on any CalDAV server. Provider-neutral and self-hostable; Python standard library only.
servers.title: Calendar (CalDAV)
servers.tagline: See and change your events and reminders on any CalDAV calendar.

servers.name: Currency (Frankfurter)
servers.summary: Convert money and look up exchange rates, today's or historical, for about 160 currencies plus cryptocurrencies and precious metals, from Frankfurter. No API key and no account; Python standard library only.
servers.title: Currency
servers.tagline: Exchange rates for about 160 currencies, today's or any past day's.

servers.name: Discord (bot)
servers.summary: Read and post in Discord channels and threads through your own Discord bot, in the servers you add it to: catch up on a channel, post an announcement, reply in a thread. Python standard library only.
servers.title: Discord
servers.tagline: Read and post in your Discord servers through your own bot.

servers.name: Fetch Guard
servers.summary: Fetch URLs into clean, LLM-ready markdown with prompt-injection defenses
servers.title: Fetch Guard
servers.tagline: Read any web page, with defenses against instructions hidden in it.

servers.name: Filesystem MCP
servers.summary: Secure local filesystem server: read, write, search, diff, patch, and manage files
servers.title: Files
servers.tagline: Find, read, edit and organize your files.

servers.name: Git Polite
servers.summary: Git staging autopilot: line-level staging, diffs, and guided commits
servers.title: Git Polite
servers.tagline: Stage changes line by line and write commits in your Git repositories.

servers.name: GitHub (sign-in wrapper)
servers.summary: GitHub repo, issue, PR and search tools with a built-in device-flow login: no token to create or paste.
servers.title: GitHub
servers.tagline: Repos, issues, pull requests and search. Sign in from the browser, no token to paste.

servers.name: GitHub MCP (MissionSquad)
servers.summary: GitHub API server: repo/file ops, issues/PRs, search, and more
servers.title: GitHub (token)
servers.tagline: Repos, files, issues and pull requests, with a GitHub token.

servers.name: Home Assistant MCP
servers.summary: Control and query a Home Assistant instance — read entities, call services, and access automation state
servers.title: Home Assistant
servers.tagline: Control your lights, sensors and automations in Home Assistant.

servers.name: JARVIS ComfyUI — On-Device Image Generation
servers.summary: Local text-to-image generation via a running ComfyUI instance (Stable Diffusion). Queues a generation workflow, polls until completion, writes the output PNG to disk and returns its file path plus small metadata (dimensions, prompt_id) — the image bytes are never inlined into the result. Entirely on-device, no cloud API, no data leaves the machine. GPU-dependent: requires a model checkpoint loaded in ComfyUI.
servers.title: ComfyUI
servers.tagline: Make images on your own computer with Stable Diffusion.

servers.name: JARVIS Computer Use — Linux
servers.summary: Local Wayland/KDE Plasma desktop control via AT-SPI2 accessibility (read windows, find and click elements, set text in form fields) and ydotool (keyboard injection, mouse clicks, key sequences). Screenshots via Spectacle or grim. Semantic AT-SPI actions are preferred over raw coordinates; raw input is available for apps with no accessibility tree. All input-injection tools are DANGEROUS-tier and must route through JARVIS TLA confirmation. Screenshot capture is ELEVATED-tier (screen content may include passwords or private data).
servers.title: Computer Use
servers.tagline: See and use the windows on your KDE Plasma desktop: read, click and type.

servers.name: JARVIS Email
servers.summary: Personal email over plain IMAP and SMTP: list mailboxes, search, read, and send from the user's own account. Provider-neutral — any IMAP/SMTP host, no vendor API and no OAuth broker; credentials stay on the machine. Mail is untrusted third-party text: every read result carries a provenance banner, attachments are listed but never decoded, and send_message is an irreversible outward-facing action.
servers.title: Email
servers.tagline: Search, read and send email from your own account, with any provider.

servers.name: JARVIS Shell
servers.summary: Run commands as the logged-in user on the computer JARVIS runs on, no root or password needed: quick system update checks that list available package updates (checkupdates, pacman -Qu, apt list --upgradable, dnf check-update), reading logs and service status, and running programs and scripts. Interactive commands run as named PTY jobs answerable mid-run via send_input; files, URLs and apps open in the desktop session. No sudo: applying updates, installing packages and other privileged commands go to jarvis-shell-system-mcp.
servers.title: Shell
servers.tagline: Run commands as you, no password needed.

servers.name: JARVIS Shell (System)
servers.summary: Run commands as root on the computer JARVIS runs on: applying system updates and upgrades (pacman -Syu, apt upgrade, dnf upgrade), installing and removing packages, starting, stopping and restarting systemd services, and other administrator work; every command asks for the administrator password. Only checking whether updates exist needs no root (jarvis-shell-mcp). Installed to /usr/share/mcp; interactive commands (a package manager's [Y/n]) run as named PTY jobs answerable mid-run via send_input
servers.title: Shell as root
servers.tagline: Run commands as root after your password: updates, installs, services.

servers.name: Maps (OpenStreetMap)
servers.summary: Find places and addresses, search what is nearby, and get routes with distance and travel time by car, bike or foot, from OpenStreetMap. No API key and no account; Python standard library only.
servers.title: Maps
servers.tagline: Find places, see what's nearby and get routes by car, bike or foot.

servers.name: Media Control (MPRIS)
servers.summary: Play, pause, skip, seek and set volume on any local media player over MPRIS, and report what is playing. Entirely local -- no account, no API key, no network.
servers.title: Media Control
servers.tagline: Play, pause, skip and set the volume in whatever is playing.

servers.name: Microsoft 365
servers.summary: Outlook mail and calendar, OneDrive, contacts, To Do and OneNote in your Microsoft account, with a built-in Microsoft sign-in
servers.title: Microsoft 365
servers.tagline: Outlook mail and calendar, OneDrive, To Do and OneNote, with a Microsoft sign-in.

servers.name: n8n-MCP
servers.summary: Build and manage n8n workflow automations: search 500+ n8n nodes, validate workflow JSON, and (with an API URL + key) create, update, delete, test and inspect workflows, executions and credentials on the user's own n8n instance. Node documentation is served from a bundled SQLite database; the management tools talk to a live n8n instance whose workflow definitions, execution data and community templates are untrusted third-party content.
servers.title: n8n
servers.tagline: Build and run n8n workflow automations.

servers.name: News
servers.summary: Latest headlines from major news outlets' feeds, and recent articles about any topic from the GDELT Project's worldwide index. No API key and no account; Python standard library only.
servers.title: News
servers.tagline: Today's headlines, and recent stories on any topic from around the world.

servers.name: Notion
servers.summary: Search, read and edit your Notion pages, databases and task lists, through Notion's official hosted server with a browser sign-in
servers.title: Notion
servers.tagline: Search, read and edit your Notion pages and databases.

servers.name: Obsidian Vault MCP
servers.summary: Read, write, and search notes in an Obsidian vault — local file I/O only, no network egress
servers.title: Obsidian
servers.tagline: Read, write and search the notes in your Obsidian vault.

servers.name: Playwright Browser
servers.summary: Interactive browser automation via accessibility-tree snapshots: navigate, click, type, fill forms, take screenshots, manage tabs. Deterministic — acts on the structured a11y tree, not pixel-guessing; headless-capable. Web page content is untrusted input: outputs flow through JARVIS's Cryptographic Boundary Protocol and dangerous actions gate through TLA.
servers.title: Playwright Browser
servers.tagline: Open pages in a real browser, click through them and fill in forms.

servers.name: Sequential Thinking MCP
servers.summary: Structured step-by-step reasoning scaffold. The calling model records one thought at a time -- with running thoughtNumber/totalThoughts and optional revision and branching -- and the tool echoes each step back with progress counters. A pure reasoning aid: it operates only on thoughts the caller supplies and has no filesystem, network, or code-execution surface.
servers.title: Sequential Thinking
servers.tagline: Helps the AI work a hard problem through one step at a time.

servers.name: Slack MCP
servers.summary: Read channels and post messages to Slack via bot token — requires scoped bot OAuth credentials
servers.title: Slack
servers.tagline: Read channels and post messages in Slack.

servers.name: SQLite MCP
servers.summary: Expose a local SQLite database for schema inspection and SQL querying
servers.title: SQLite
servers.tagline: Look inside a SQLite database and query it.

servers.name: System Status
servers.summary: System information and health for the machine JARVIS runs on: OS and package manager, battery, CPU, memory, disk, network, processes, temperatures and failed services, plus a health check that reports only what is wrong. Read-only, local, no network access.
servers.title: System Status
servers.tagline: Battery, CPU, memory, disk and temperatures, and whatever is wrong right now.

servers.name: Telegram (bot)
servers.summary: Send yourself Telegram messages and files from JARVIS, and read what you send back, through your own Telegram bot (made with @BotFather in a minute). The bot sees only messages sent to it. Python standard library only.
servers.title: Telegram
servers.tagline: Send yourself messages and files on Telegram, and read your replies.

servers.name: Time MCP
servers.summary: Time-related tools (current UTC time and Unix timestamp)
servers.title: Time
servers.tagline: The current time, to the second.

servers.name: Weather (Open-Meteo)
servers.summary: Current weather, daily and hourly forecasts, and air quality from Open-Meteo. No API key and no account; Python standard library only.
servers.title: Weather
servers.tagline: Current weather, forecasts and air quality, anywhere.

servers.name: Wikipedia
servers.summary: Search Wikipedia and read article summaries, full articles by section, and what happened on this day in history, in any language. No API key and no account; Python standard library only.
servers.title: Wikipedia
servers.tagline: Search and read Wikipedia in any language, and what happened on this day.
